name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.14.2 — three `review.md` prose corrections, found by /spec:review of the driver spine's own spec (JJ + Fable 5 consult, 2026-08-21). The frozen-base check + detached-worktree add/remove, cut at build time, is retired outright rather than deferred: attributing foreign hunks to their owning spec (the driver's skip-name extraction) covers both the HEAD-moved-past case the mechanism targeted and the interleaved-concurrent case it structurally cannot see, so `review.md`'s false claim that the driver runs the check is removed and § Protocol now names the base-derivation rungs that actually shipped (`build_base` → `diff_base` → `merge-base HEAD main|master`). The `done`-spec re-run promise is retired: re-reviewing a `done` spec was walking the full stage with zero ledger append and zero retained evidence (`runId: undefined`), so a cold invocation on an already-closed spec is now refused (exit 2), pointing at `/spec:escape` — the command for a defect that escaped a review that already passed. The CLOSE step's close-commit text is corrected for worktree reviews: `.claude/spec-runs.jsonl` and `.claude/spec-runs/` are excluded from the close commit and promoted to the main root once the merge lands, since committing them inside the worktree left `merge-back cleanup` seeing a dirty tree and exiting 2 after the merge had already landed; in-place reviews are unaffected. 7.14.1 — smoke serializes behind every leg that can run host tests or build the app: `review-legs.js` wave 2 ran `smoke.sh` concurrently with the at-risk test dispatch and the patterns sweep, and a host at-risk test performing a real production build clobbered the artifact smoke was booting (UpWell 2026-08-21, 3/3 runs: ENOTEMPTY under `.nitro/vite` during the concurrent vite build, then readyCheck never passed — smoke alone green every time). This is the same collision class the 2026-08-17 wave-1 comment already documented for the gate, so smoke now runs in its own wave after at-risk/patterns/drift complete; two observed members, so an in-place fix, not a standing guard. Second defect from the same report: smoke's stdout/stderr were discarded entirely — a red smoke row carried no diagnosis and cost two extra full re-runs to identify — so the full output now lands in `<out-dir>/smoke.txt`, advertised on the outputs line. Pinned by a behavioral test whose fixture at-risk run sleeps then drops a marker the bootCommand probes for at boot start — red on the pre-fix concurrency by construction (verified against the stashed pre-fix script). 7.14.0 — review becomes a driver-stepped program, the shape `/spec:design` already proved: a new `spec-review-driver.js` (`spec-paths review-driver`) owns the review stage's sequencing — base derivation, the per-iteration evidence manifest, `review-legs.js`, diffLoc, all three `verdict.js` passes, both ledger appends, the `implementing → done` flip, the merge-back inspect/merge/cleanup/verify sequence, `replay --due`, and the `spec-status --next` capture — executing every deterministic step itself and refusing to advance past an unverified mark: a missing or malformed reviewer return file, a `REVIEWER_FAILED` verdict, disposition counts exceeding the survivor+leg-finding pools, or a `closed` mark on a dirty tree all exit 2 with the state left unchanged. A `RED_BLOCKING` gate failure now lands the terminal state `STOPPED` with the `GATE_RED` ledger line already appended by the driver itself, closing what used to be a prose duty the session could forget; the fix loop's 2-iteration cap is enforced by the driver counting the manifest files actually present on disk, not a stored counter, so a third `fix-applied` is structurally unreachable rather than merely discouraged. `review.md` shrinks to the thin judgment shell this pattern established for `/spec:design`: setup, the driver-loop protocol, and the judgments the driver hands to the session — reviewer and design-leg dispatch, dispositions, canonical-delta application, merge strategy, conflict resolution — with every choreography paragraph the driver now executes deleted from the command file. Motivation: review had the most hand-performed deterministic steps (~14) of any stage, wrapped around the pipeline's most safety-critical derivations, and procedural hallucination — skipping or fabricating a required step while reporting success — is the measured largest agent-failure class (38.5%, agenticrail.nz 2026-08-08); a driver-owned sequence eliminates the failure mode structurally instead of auditing for it after the fact. `spec/entrypoints.json` gains the driver's entry and its five script-to-script edges in the same diff, pushing the manifest to roughly 17 edges — past spec 04 D12's dozen-edge successor trigger, deliberately deferred and recorded here rather than silently, since the growth is hub-shaped (one new caller), per-edge declaration keeps 04's rename detection, and the honest re-evaluation point is the build/plan drivers becoming the next such hubs.
